newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec consumer credit rose $4.9 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec consumer credit rose $4.9 billion.

text.p: U.S. consumer credit grew $4.9 billion in December at a 4.9 percent annual rate after rising a revised $5.1 billion in November at a 5.1 percent annual rate, the Federal Reserve said Friday
Wall Street analysts had forecast that December consumer credit would rise more strongly by $6.7 billion.
Previously the Fed said November consumer credit had increased by $7.4 billion but it revised that down.
During December, growth in revolving, or credit-card credit, slowed to a $2.4-billion rise at a 6.2 percent annual rate from $4 billion at a 10.6 percent rate in November.
But auto credit outstanding picked up to a $600 million rise at a 1.9 percent annual rate in December after falling in November by $100 million at a 0.3 percent annual rate.

Other credit, which includes consumer bank loans like those for mobile homes and to pay for education but not real estate mortgages, grew by $1.8 billion at a 6.3 percent annual rate in December. That was up from November when this category of credit advanced $1.2 billion at a 3.9 percent annual rate.
Before seasonal adjustment, total outstanding consumer credit in December was $1.23 trillion, up from $1.13 trillion a year earlier in December 1995.
